prompt.context_jp: 派遣という身でありながら、その働きぶり___相変わらず群を抜いていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 派遣という身でありながら、その働きぶり___相変わらず群を抜いていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that fits this contrastive topic.

feedback.correct_en: は marks 働きぶり as the contrastive topic — 'as for her work performance (despite being a temp)…'. The clause sets up a contrast with her lowly status.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would introduce 働きぶり as new information, but here it's the discussed subject being contrasted against her position.

contrast_examples.jp: 見た目は地味だが、実力は抜群だ。
contrast_examples.en: She looks plain, but her ability is outstanding.

contrast_examples.jp: 急に働きぶりが落ちた。

prompt.context_jp: 小さな節約___会社の大きな利益に直結するのだよ
prompt.prompt_jp: 小さな節約___会社の大きな利益に直結するのだよ
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that fits the topic in this generic statement.

feedback.correct_en: は marks the topic for a general claim: 'small savings (as a rule) lead directly to big profits.'
feedback.incorrect_en: が would point to a specific instance of saving as news, but this is a proverb-like generalization.

prompt.context_jp: 今 わが社の業績___芳しくないのは 分かってるね？
prompt.prompt_jp: 今 わが社の業績___芳しくないのは 分かってるね？
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle inside the の-clause.

feedback.correct_en: Inside a subordinate の/こと clause, the subject typically takes が. The whole clause 業績が芳しくない is then topicalized by のは.
feedback.incorrect_en: は inside the embedded clause would create a double-topic structure that sounds unnatural here.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼が来ないのは残念だ。
contrast_examples.en: It's a shame that he isn't coming.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼は来ないのが残念だ。
contrast_examples.en: As for him, his not coming is a shame (odd/marked).

prompt.context_jp: 東海林君 Ｓ＆Ｆの命運___懸かっているんだ！
prompt.prompt_jp: Ｓ＆Ｆの命運___懸かっているんだ！
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that emphasizes what is at stake.

feedback.correct_en: が presents 命運 as the dramatic new information — 'the very fate of S&F is on the line!' It carries the emotional weight of a reveal.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make 命運 a mere topic, flattening the urgency the president wants to convey.

contrast_examples.jp: 君の未来がかかっている!

prompt.context_jp: 今 俺の背中に吹いてる追い風___計測不能と言っていいよ
prompt.prompt_jp: 俺の背中に吹いてる追い風___計測不能と言っていいよ
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle fitting a description-of-topic structure.

feedback.correct_en: は topicalizes 追い風 so Shoji can comment on it: 'as for the tailwind at my back, it's immeasurable.' Classic 'X は Y だ' description.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make it a sudden announcement of a new subject, but here he's elaborating on a known situation.

contrast_examples.en: Suddenly a wind started blowing (new event).

prompt.context_jp: 派遣として幾多の職場を渡り歩いてきた大前ほど、傾きかけた会社の兆候に敏感な者___いない。
prompt.prompt_jp: 大前ほど、傾きかけた会社の兆候に敏感な者___いない。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for the 'no one X-er than Y' pattern.

feedback.correct_en: In the 'X ほど ... 者はいない' pattern (no one is more X than Y), は is required with いない in the negative existential.
feedback.incorrect_en: が者 would undo the fixed idiomatic pattern used for superlative comparisons.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼ほど優しい人はいない。
contrast_examples.en: No one is kinder than he is.
There are no kind people (plain negative).

prompt.context_jp: 消耗品や備品を 急に けちりだした会社___黄色信号です
prompt.prompt_jp: 消耗品や備品を急にけちりだした会社___黄色信号です
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for the classifying judgement.

feedback.correct_en: は marks the described-noun topic in the 'X は Y だ' classification: 'companies that suddenly cut supplies — those are a yellow flag.'
feedback.incorrect_en: が would announce the company as new info, but Omae is making a generic categorization.

contrast_examples.jp: 急に値上げする店は危ない。
contrast_examples.en: Shops that suddenly raise prices are dangerous.

prompt.context_jp: 今や 派遣なしに 会社___回らない
prompt.prompt_jp: 今や 派遣なしに 会社___回らない
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for the generic statement.

feedback.correct_en: は marks 会社 as the generic topic — companies (in general, these days) can't run without temps.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would spotlight one specific company as news, but this is a broad narrator-style claim.

prompt.context_jp: 彼女の辞書に “不可能”と“残業”の文字___ない
prompt.prompt_jp: 彼女の辞書に“不可能”と“残業”の文字___ない
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for the existential subject.

feedback.correct_en: With ある/ない negative existence, the thing that doesn't exist is marked by は when the sentence asserts absence as a defining trait: 'the words don't exist (in her dictionary).'
feedback.incorrect_en: が would simply report the absence neutrally; は here adds contrastive emphasis fitting the dramatic narration style.

contrast_examples.jp: 私の辞書に不可能の文字はない。
contrast_examples.en: The word 'impossible' is not in my dictionary (famous phrasing).

prompt.context_jp: だが スーパーハケン 大前春子___なぜ 非正規社員の道を選んだかは 定かでない
prompt.prompt_jp: スーパーハケン 大前春子___なぜ 非正規社員の道を選んだかは 定かでない
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for the subject inside the embedded question.

feedback.correct_en: The subject of an embedded indirect question (なぜ…選んだか) takes が. The whole clause is then topicalized by は at the end.
feedback.incorrect_en: は inside the embedded question creates a competing topic that clashes with the outer のは.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼が何を考えているかは分からない。

contrast_examples.en: As for him, his thoughts can't be read.

prompt.context_jp: 気付けば、机の周りから里中の姿___すっかり消えていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 机の周りから里中の姿___すっかり消えていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that fits this noticing-event.

feedback.correct_en: が marks 里中の姿 as new information noticed by the viewpoint character — a sudden realization that Satonaka is gone.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would presuppose Satonaka's figure as the established topic and comment on it, losing the 'I just noticed' nuance.

contrast_examples.jp: 見れば、財布がなくなっていた。
contrast_examples.en: When I looked, my wallet was gone (discovery).
The wallet is on the desk (topic comment).

prompt.context_jp: 経木___通気性がいい上に 余分な水分を 吸い取ってくれるんで
prompt.prompt_jp: 経木___通気性がいい上に 余分な水分を 吸い取ってくれる
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for the explanatory topic.

feedback.correct_en: は marks 経木 as the topic being explained — 'as for cedar wood sheets, they are breathable and absorb moisture.'
feedback.incorrect_en: が would signal 経木 as a fresh discovery, but Sumida is defining a known material.

prompt.context_jp: あっけないほど古いパスワード___、東海林は思わず苦笑を漏らした。
prompt.prompt_jp: あっけないほど古いパスワード___、東海林は思わず苦笑を漏らした。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that marks the stimulus of a reaction.

feedback.correct_en: に marks the stimulus/target of an emotional reaction — he smiled wryly AT the password.
feedback.incorrect_en: で would mean 'by means of/at the location of' the password. を is wrong because 苦笑を漏らす already takes 苦笑 as its object.

contrast_examples.en: I was surprised at his words.

prompt.context_jp: このメールを送ったの___僕なんです
prompt.prompt_jp: このメールを送ったの___僕なんです
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle in the cleft 'the one who X is Y' structure.

feedback.correct_en: In the cleft pattern 'Xたのは Yだ' (the one who did X is Y), は is required to topicalize the の-nominalized clause.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would break the cleft structure; the pattern fixes は after のnominalization.

prompt.context_jp: 派遣___切られる時は切られる じたばたしたって無駄
prompt.prompt_jp: 派遣___切られる時は切られる
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle fitting Omae's generic statement about temps.

feedback.correct_en: は marks 派遣 as the general topic — temps as a category get cut when they get cut. It's a philosophical generalization.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would spotlight specific temps getting cut, but Omae is making a detached rule-of-life statement.

prompt.context_jp: 一度 使っても ___ が残っている限り もう一度 使ってもらいたい
prompt.prompt_jp: 付箋を一度 使っても ___ が残っている限り もう一度 使ってもらいたい
prompt.prompt_en: Fill the blank describing why a sticky note can be reused.

feedback.correct_en: 粘着力 (nenchakuryoku) is the standard word for adhesive/sticking power of tape or sticky notes.
feedback.incorrect_en: 付着力 and 接続力 exist but refer to adhesion in physics or connection power — not the everyday word for sticky-note stickiness.

contrast_examples.jp: このテープは粘着力が強い。
contrast_examples.en: This tape has strong adhesive power.

contrast_examples.jp: ネットワークの接続力

prompt.context_jp: “___ も積もれば山となる” 小さな節約は 会社の大きな利益に直結するのだよ
prompt.prompt_jp: “___ も積もれば山となる”
prompt.prompt_en: Complete this famous Japanese proverb.

feedback.correct_en: 塵も積もれば山となる — 'even dust piled up becomes a mountain', the standard proverb meaning small things add up.
feedback.incorrect_en: 砂 and 水 don't appear in this fixed proverb; it has only one accepted wording.

contrast_examples.jp: 塵も積もれば山となる。
contrast_examples.en: Small things add up to great things.
A journey of a thousand miles begins with one step.

prompt.context_jp: 大丈夫だ 諸君 ___ に乗ったつもりで 俺についてきてくれ
prompt.prompt_jp: ___ に乗ったつもりで 俺についてきてくれ
prompt.prompt_en: Complete the idiom 'trust me, you're in good hands.'

feedback.correct_en: 大船に乗ったつもりで is the set idiom — 'as if you're aboard a big ship', meaning 'rest assured, you're safe with me.'
feedback.incorrect_en: 大波 (big wave) would mean the opposite — being in danger. 大舟 is a wrong spelling.

contrast_examples.jp: 大船に乗ったつもりで任せてください。
contrast_examples.en: Leave it to me with full confidence.
To be swallowed by a big wave (danger).

prompt.context_jp: “大前っち”と なれなれしく呼ぶのは 金輪際やめてください！ ___ が立ちました
prompt.prompt_jp: ___ が立ちました
prompt.prompt_en: Which word completes 'I got ___' expressing creepy disgust?

feedback.correct_en: 鳥肌が立つ (literally 'bird skin stands up') is the idiom for getting goosebumps from disgust, awe, or chill.
feedback.incorrect_en: 冷汗 collocates with 出る ('cold sweat breaks out'), not 立つ. 羽毛 (down/feathers) is not idiomatic.

contrast_examples.en: It was so scary I got goosebumps.
I broke into a cold sweat.

prompt.context_jp: 会社が期待しているのは もっと大胆な ___ だよ
prompt.prompt_jp: もっと大胆な ___ だよ
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the metaphor for drastic cost-cutting.

feedback.correct_en: 大ナタを振るう ('swing a big machete') is the idiom for making drastic, bold cuts — exactly the drastic restructuring the exec demands.
feedback.incorrect_en: 大太鼓 (big drum) and 大判 (big coin/oval) have no connection to restructuring.

contrast_examples.jp: 人員に大ナタを振るう。

prompt.context_jp: だから それがコスト高なんだ ___ って 賢ちゃん
prompt.prompt_jp: ___ って 賢ちゃん
prompt.prompt_en: Which adjective fits 'you're too naive/soft'?

feedback.correct_en: 甘い here means 'naive / too soft-hearted.' Shoji is scolding Ken for being idealistic about costs.
feedback.incorrect_en: 辛い (harsh/painful) and 緩い (loose) don't convey this 'overly idealistic' meaning in this context.

prompt.context_jp: 今使っている 木の弁当箱の ___ がなくなり次第 こちらのプラスチックのものに 切り替えてください
prompt.prompt_jp: 木の弁当箱の ___ がなくなり次第
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the business term for 'stock on hand'.

feedback.correct_en: 在庫 is inventory/stock. '在庫がなくなり次第' = 'as soon as stock runs out' is standard business Japanese.
feedback.incorrect_en: 残高 means account balance; 残業 means overtime work. Neither fits physical stock.

contrast_examples.jp: 口座の残高を確認する。

prompt.context_jp: ___ なら 仕方ありませんね
prompt.prompt_jp: ___ なら 仕方ありませんね
prompt.prompt_en: Omae grudgingly accepts. Which phrase fits?

feedback.correct_en: 業務命令 = 'a work order from above.' Omae reluctantly agrees only because it's framed as an official order.
feedback.incorrect_en: 業務連絡 is just a work announcement; 業務時間 is working hours. Neither forces compliance.

contrast_examples.jp: 業務命令なので従います。
contrast_examples.en: I'll comply since it's an order.

prompt.context_jp: Omae is asked what she's doing at the copier. Which response sounds most like her signature clipped professional style?
prompt.prompt_en: Which line fits Omae's trademark deadpan register?

choices.text: 見てのとおり 紙の補充ですが 何か？
見ればわかるでしょう、紙を入れてるんです。

feedback.correct_en: '〜ですが 何か？' is Omae's catchphrase register — polite ます/です surface with an aggressively cool challenge. Matches her character.
feedback.incorrect_en: B sounds snippy but normal; C is too casual/fragmented. Neither captures her distinctive polite-but-icy tone.

contrast_examples.jp: 見てのとおり作業中ですが、何か？
contrast_examples.en: As you can see, I'm working. Problem?

prompt.context_jp: Satonaka advises Shoji to just ask Omae for help honestly. Which phrasing sounds most natural for a close colleague nudging a friend?
prompt.prompt_en: Which sounds most natural for this friendly nudge?

choices.text: 素直に 大前さんに 手伝ってほしいって言いなよ
正直に大前さんに手伝ってほしいと申してください
大前さんに手伝いなさいと言え

feedback.correct_en: 〜言いなよ is a soft, friendly imperative fitting close-friend register, and 素直に captures 'just be honest' naturally.
feedback.incorrect_en: B mixes humble 申す with a command — register clash. C is a blunt order that doesn't fit the gentle nudge.

contrast_examples.jp: 手伝ってって頼みなよ。

prompt.context_jp: Omae coolly tells Konatsu not to fret about AI. Which phrasing best matches her blunt philosophical tone?
prompt.prompt_en: Which version sounds most like Omae's style?

choices.text: 派遣は 切られる時は切られる じたばたしたって無駄
派遣の方々も切られる時はお切られになりますよ
派遣が切られることもあるかもしれないので、気を付けたほうがいいですよ

feedback.correct_en: The fatalistic 'X時はX' pattern plus じたばたしても無駄 delivers Omae's cool, terse worldview perfectly.
feedback.incorrect_en: B invents incorrect keigo (お切られになる is not well-formed). C is wordy and hedged — opposite of Omae's style.

contrast_examples.en: When it's no good, it's no good.

contrast_examples.jp: もしかしたらダメかもしれません。
contrast_examples.en: It might possibly be no good (hedged).

prompt.context_jp: Satonaka must tell Sumida that Magokoro Bento has to change. Which phrasing sounds most natural for this painful business delivery?
prompt.prompt_en: Which is the most natural, appropriately-formal apology?

choices.text: ただ… まごころ弁当を 変えていかなくてはいけません
でもまごころ弁当は変えないとダメです
まごころ弁当を変えないといけないのです、すみません

feedback.correct_en: ただ… softens the bad news, and 変えていかなくてはいけません carries formal necessity without being harsh — exactly right for an apologetic business delivery.
feedback.incorrect_en: B's ダメです is too casual for a formal supplier meeting. C front-loads the issue bluntly and tacks on すみません awkwardly.

contrast_examples.jp: ただ、変更せざるを得ません。
contrast_examples.en: However, we have no choice but to change (formal).

prompt.context_jp: The Sumida Foods president welcomes the visiting team. Which greeting sounds most natural for a supplier receiving business guests?
prompt.prompt_en: Which supplier-greeting sounds most natural?

choices.text: お世話になっております あっ 夏の新メニュー どうぞ 皆さんで 召し上がってみてください
お疲れさまです。新メニューです。食べてください
こんにちは、新メニューをみんなで食べてね

feedback.correct_en: お世話になっております is the standard B2B greeting, and 召し上がってみてください is appropriately polite 尊敬語 for offering food to guests.
feedback.incorrect_en: B's 食べてください and お疲れさまです are too casual/inappropriate for a first greeting to clients. C drops into タメ口 ('食べてね') which is wrong with clients.

contrast_examples.jp: お世話になっております。どうぞ召し上がってください。
contrast_examples.en: Thank you for your business. Please help yourself.
Go ahead and eat (casual with friends).
